newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-day depos swing, zloty calm at resistance.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-day depos swing, zloty calm at resistance.

text.p: Polish one-day deposit rates tumbled in early trade as banks cut short-term positions ahead of the end of February's reserve period only to rebound after the central bank offered a large cash drainage, dealers said.

Overnight rates plunged more than ten points after opening above 21 percent but then rates bounced back to around 20 percent after the National Bank of Poland stepped in with a two billion zloty reverse repo offer for two, seven and 14 days.
"Rates jumped back after the NBP announced its huge drainage but uncertainty about future rate moves remained as banks had different positions," said Piotr Kiegel from BOS SA.

At 1020 GMT overnight rates were at 20.00/21.50 percent against the opaning's 21.00/21.40 with morning transactions bottoming out around 10 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 20.00/21.50 percent against opening's 21.35/21.55 percent.

Dealers who expcted that most banks had long positions said rates may fall ahead of the close end of February's reserve on Thursday, but others said rates may stay above 20 percent as banks still needed to fine-tune reserve accounts.
The NBP drainage pushed up O/N rates despite tomorrow's settlement date because players used the relatively cheap cash to build up reserves, dealers said.
